messages:
Matt H: Heads up — seeing an OOB session fanout from prov-runner into us-central1. GPU nodes being evicted due to jump-host saturation.
ops-bot: ALERT: ipmi-session-flood detected on rack-rg4 (us-central1-a) — ~2.2k sessions/min, jump-host conn pool exhausted :rotating_light:
Sara P: Ugh. Was there a firmware push recently? any correlation with microcode/BIOS/BMC updates?
Matt H: Yes — we rolled microcode v2.1.4 to ~60% of us-central last night around 02:00 UTC. Initial hypothesis: BMC agent restart is creating reconnect loops to kvm-proxy.
Kevin L: Can you paste a quick sample of the session table?
Matt H: Sure — grabbed a snippet from jump-host:
```
# ss -tnp | grep kvm-proxy | wc -l
2200
# ss -tnp | grep '10.10.42.' | head -n 5
ESTAB 0 0 10.10.42.12:623 10.0.1.4:51022 users:("kvm-proxy",pid=442)
ESTAB 0 0 10.10.42.13:623 10.0.1.4:51023 users:("kvm-proxy",pid=442)
...
```
Lina (oncall): If jump-host conn pool is exhausted, prov-runner starts retrying and rapidly reprovisions. We should throttle provisioning and stop the rollout.
Sara P: Agreed. Can we pause the microcode rollout and start a rollback on the affected racks? Also reduce prov concurrency.
Matt H: Initiating rollback for rack-rg4 and nearby racks in us-central1-a now. Launching rollback job to v2.1.3.
deploy-bot: rollback-job/1717774444 started — targets: rack-rg4 (40 hosts) :rocket:
Kevin L: Short-term mitigation: add max_conn cap on ipmi proxy and increase BMC keepalive from 10s -> 60s. Also add a per-source rate limit on jump-hosts. I'll open a quick CL (PR #1234).
Lina (oncall): Running provctl to throttle concurrency: `provctl throttle --rack rack-rg4 --concurrency 2`
Matt H: provctl executed. Monitoring: jump-host conn count dropping — now ~800 and evictions in GPU pool falling.
Sara P: Cost note: we estimate ~8k in extra reprovisioning + preemptible churn over last 4 hours. Logging cost hit to incident.
Matt H: Root-cause guess: microcode flash toggled a secureboot flag intermittently which triggers the management agent to restart and renegotiate sessions. Need vendor confirmation.
Lina (oncall): If rollback doesn't clear within 30m I'll escalate to vendor support (p0). Also can we gate future BMC pushes behind a keepalive/canary test (no more than 5 hosts simultaneously)?
Kevin L: Will add a preflight to rollout tooling: simulate BMC reboot and validate session stabilizes for 5m before wider rollout. Follow-up CL to add rate-limit param to rollout orchestration.
Matt H: Thanks — monitoring charts look better. @everyone please avoid touching BMC images in us-central until we finish validation. :exclamation:
Sara P: Noted. I'll update the runbook: steps to check jump-host conn table, how to throttle provctl, and rollback commands.
Lina (oncall): I'll keep watch for 1hr and then reopen a postmortem if rollback doesn't fully restore capacity.
Kevin L: Filed PR for tool changes and vendor repro steps.
Matt H: Closing loop — rollback completed on rack-rg4 at +18m, GPU pool returning to steady state. Continuing slow canary for the rest of us-central.
ops-bot: RESOLVED: ipmi-session-flood on rack-rg4 — connections dropped below threshold.
Sara P: Great work team. Add follow-up action: add session caps to jump-hosts and add a billing-tag for firmware rollouts so cost impacts are easier to track.
Lina (oncall): Copy. I'm adding this to oncall checklist.
Matt H: Thanks all — will follow up with the postmortem doc and vendor ticket link."
